Notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as the "Act of 1894") for therebys bringing the subject lands to acquisition became issued on 03.08.1999 (Annexure P-3).
The said notification, became succeeded by a declaration made on 15.02.2000 (Annexure P-4), thus under Section 6 of the Act of 1894.

An award dated 14.02.2002 (Annexure P-5)
became rendered in pursuance thereto, thus its rendition occurred prior to the institution of the CWP-7898- 2000 by the present non-applicant-petitioner before this Court.
The said writ petition was dismissed by this Court, on 20.04.2011 (Annexure P-8).

The dismissal verdict (supra), as made on the writ petition (supra) led the 1 of 12 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:085272-DB aggrieved-petitioner to institute SLP bearing No.31560-2011 before the Hon'ble Apex Court, but the said SLP became dismissed on 02.12.2011.

The said relief became banked upon the provisions carried in Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation And Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as the "Act of 2013").

sentences.text: The relief on the basis of the said statutory provision became anviled on the factum, that neither rapat possession has been assumed over the subject lands nor the compensation as determined under the award (supra), was made available for disbursement to the land-losers concerned.

3. Through a verdict made on the said writ petition, on 29.11.2016, the writ petition was allowed and the impugned acquisition was declared to have become lapsed in terms of Section 24(2) of the Act of 2013.
The verdict (supra) led the aggrieved-U.T. to institute SLP bearing No.SLP (Civil) No.5409 of 2018, before the Hon'ble Apex Court.
On the said SLP, the hereinafter extracted order became pronounced on 19.02.2018.
"Heard.
Delay condoned.

In view of the judgment of this court in Civil Appeal No.20982 of 2017 "Indore Development Authority V. Shailendra (dead) through its LRs & others" and connected matters, the petitioner is at liberty to seek review of the impugned judgment in accordance with law.
The special leave petition is disposed of accordingly.

Pending applications if any shall also stand disposed of"
2 of 12 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:085272-DB 4.
In terms of the said order passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court on the SLP (supra), the present applicant-U.T., has instituted the instant review application.

5. Since the verdict made by this Court, on 29.11.2016 was banked upon a judgment made, by the Apex Court in case "Pune Municipal Corporation and Another V. Harakchand Missirmal Solanki and others"
reported in (2014) 3 Supreme Court Cases 183, whereas, with the said judgment becoming reversed by a verdict rendered by the Constitutional Bench of the Apex Court, thus in Civil Appeal No.20982-2017, titled as "Indore Development Authority V. Shailendra (dead) through its LRs and others".

6. Consequently, it becomes incumbent upon this Court to, after culling out the expostulations of law made by Constitutional Bench of the Apex Court, in the verdict rendered in Indore Development Shaheed Baba Jiwan Singh Ji vs U.T Chandigarh And Anr on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7397259/
2 case (supra), thus to subsequently apply the said made expostulations of law to the facts available at hand.

sentences.text: 7. The learned counsel appearing for the non-applicant-petitioner submits, that the expostulations of law, as carried in paragraph No.99 and 363 of the said judgment rendered by the Constitutional Bench of Hon'ble Apex Court in Indore Development case (supra), paragraphs whereof become extracted hereinafter, thus unfold qua the thereins, occurring word "or" between possession and compensation, has been read as "nor" or "and".

Resultantly he submits that any one of the two parameters, respectively relating to availability of compensation to the land-losers concerned, and assumption of rapat possession over the subject lands, thus was required to 3 of 12 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:085272-DB be established.
Therefore, when evidently one of the parameter (supra), has been satisfied, thereupon no lapsing declaration can be made.
"99. In this Court's considered view, as regards the collation of the words used in Section 24(2), two negative conditions have been prescribed.
Thus, even if one condition is satisfied, there is no lapse, and this logically flows from the Act of 1894 read with the provisions of Section 24 of the Act of 2013.
Any other interpretation would entail illogical results.
That apart, if the rule of interpretation with respect to two negative conditions qualified by "or" is used, then "or" should be read as "nor" or "and".

Brown & Co. v. Harrison (supra), ruled thus, about the interpretation of two negative conditions connected by the word "or":
".....I think it quite commonly and grammatically can have a conjunctive sense.

It is generally disjunctive, but it may be plain from the collation of words that it is meant in a conjunctive sense, and certainly where the use of the word as a disjunctive leads to repugnance or absurdity, it is quite within the ordinary principles of construction adopted by the court to give the word a conjunctive use.

Here, it is quite plain that the word leads to an absurdity, because the contention put forward by the shipowners in this matter amounts to this, as my Lord said, that, if a shipowner himself breaks open a case and steals the contents of it, he is exempted from liability under r 2(q) if none of his servants stole the part of the case or broke it open.
That seems to me to be a plain absurdity.
In addition to that, there is a repugnancy because it is plainly repugnant to the second part of r 2(q).
Therefore I say no more about that."
xxx 363.

In view of the aforesaid discussion, we answer the questions as under:
1. Under the provisions of Section 24(1)(a) in case the award is not made as on 1.1.2014 the date of commencement of Act of 2013, there is no lapse of proceedings.
Compensation has to be determined under the provisions of Act of 2013.

2. In case the award has been passed within the window period of five years excluding the period covered by an interim order of the court, then proceedings shall continue Shaheed Baba Jiwan Singh Ji vs U.T Chandigarh And Anr on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7397259/

3. The word 'or' used in Section 24(2) between possession and compensation has to be read as 'nor' or as 'and'.

The deemed lapse of land acquisition proceedings under Section 24(2) of the Act of 2013 takes place where due to inaction of authorities for five years or more prior to commencement of the said Act, the possession of land has not been taken nor compensation has been paid.
In other words, in case possession has been taken, compensation has not been paid then there is no lapse.
Similarly, if compensation has been paid, possession has not been taken then there is no lapse.
4. The expression 'paid' in the main part of Section 24(2) of the Act of 2013 does not include a deposit of compensation in court.
The consequence of non-deposit is provided in proviso to Section 24(2)

in case it has not been deposited with respect to majority of land holdings then all beneficiaries (landowners) as on the date of notification for land acquisition under Section 4 of the Act of 1894 shall be entitled to compensation in accordance with the provisions of the Act of 2013.
In case the obligation under Section 31 of the Land Acquisition Act of 1894 has not been fulfilled, interest under Section 34 of the said Act can be granted.
Non-deposit of compensation (in court) does not result in the lapse of land acquisition proceedings.

In case of non-deposit with respect to the majority of holdings for five years or more, compensation under the Act of 2013 has to be paid to the "landowners"as on the date of notification for land acquisition under Section 4 of the Act of 1894.

5. In case a person has been tendered the compensation as provided under Section 31(1) of the Act of 1894, it is not open to him to claim that acquisition has lapsed under Section 24(2) due to non- payment or non-deposit of compensation in court.
The obligation to pay is complete by tendering the amount under Section 31(1).Land owners
who had refused to accept compensation or who sought reference for higher compensation, cannot claim that the acquisition proceedings had lapsed under Section 24(2) of the Act of 2013.

6.The proviso to Section 24(2) of the Act of 2013 is to be treated as part of Section 24(2) not part of Section 24(1)(b).
7.

The mode of taking possession under the Act of 1894 and as 5 of 12 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:085272-DB contemplated under Section 24(2) is by drawing of inquest report/
memorandum.

Once award has been passed on taking possession under Section 16 of the Act of 1894, the land vests in State there is no divesting provided under Section 24(2) of the Act of 2013, as once possession has been taken there is no lapse under Section 24(2).

8. The provisions of Section 24(2) providing for a deemed lapse of proceedings are applicable in case authorities have failed due to their inaction to take possession and pay compensation for five years or more before the Act of 2013 came into force, in a proceeding for land acquisition pending with concerned authority as on 1.1.2014.

The period of subsistence of interim orders passed by court has Shaheed Baba Jiwan Singh Ji vs U.T Chandigarh And Anr on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7397259/
4 to be excluded in the computation of five years.

sentences.text: 9. Section 24(2) of the Act of 2013 does not give rise to new cause of action to question the legality of concluded proceedings of land acquisition.
Section 24 applies to a proceeding pending on the date of enforcement of the Act of 2013, i.e., 1.1.2014.

It does not revive stale and time-barred claims and does not reopen concluded proceedings nor allow landowners to question the legality of mode of taking possession to reopen proceedings or mode of deposit of compensation in the treasury instead of court to invalidate acquisition."
8.

Consequently, if in the first component or the segment of sub Section 2 of Section 24 of the Act of 2013, provisions whereof becomes extracted hereinafter, an expostulation is borne, thus covering a situation wherebys rather upon an award under Section 11 of the Act of 1894, becoming passed after 5 years or more before the commencement of the Act of 2013, Act whereof came into force on 01.01.2014.

However, yet the rider thereto is also expressed subsequent thereto, inasmuch as, a statutory necessity is also cast upon the acquiring authority to assume possession of the subject lands or to make available the determined compensation rather for therebys denyng the espoused lapsing declaration to the land-loser.

As stated in the hereinabove underlined relevant paragraph of the verdict made in 6 of 12 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:085272-DB Indore Development case (supra), yet the accomplishment of one of the conditions (supra) rather is sufficient to constrain Courts to decline the espoused lapsing declaration to the land-losers concerned.

"(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), in case of land acquisition proceedings initiated under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (1 of 1894),
where an award under the said section 11 has been made five years or more prior to the commencement of this Act but the physical possession of the land has not been taken or the compensation has not been paid the said proceedings shall be deemed to have lapsed and the appropriate Government, if it so chooses, shall initiate the proceedings of such land acquisition afresh in accordance with the provisions of this Act:"
9.
The further consequence thereof, has been stated to be qua the appropriate government being reserved with an option to, as such initiate fresh proceedings under the Act of 2013.

Now,
reiteratedly since the word "or" used in sub Section 2 of Section 24 of the Act of 2013, between possession and compensation, thus has been answered in Indore Development case (supra), to be readable as "nor" or as "and", besides when it has also been expostulated therein, that in case possession has been taken but compensation has been paid, thus thereupon, there is no lapse.
Moreover, if compensation has been paid but possession has not been taken, thereupon too, there is no lapse.

In sequel, reiteratedly the import of the above expostulation of law, as made in verdict (supra), is that, either possession over the subject lands is to be assumed or compensation is to be made available to be disbursed to the land-losers concerned.

Therefore, only one of the above two contingencies has to happen before coming into force of the Act of 2013.
7 of 12 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:085272-DB

Moreover, a proviso also occurs underneath sub Section 2 of Section 24 of the Act of 2013, and,
the said proviso is extracted hereinafter.

"Provided that where an award has been made and compensation in respect of a majority of land holdings has not been deposited in the account of the beneficiaries,
then, all beneficiaries specified in the notification for acquisition under section 4 of the said Land Acquisition Act, shall be entitled to compensation in accordance with the provisions of this Act."

11. A reading of the proviso occurring underneath sub Section 2 of Section 24 of the Act of 2013,
provisions whereof is also an exception thereto, discloses that in case an award has been passed under the Act of 1894 and compensation in respect of majority of landholdings, hence has not been deposited in the respective accounts of the beneficiaries, thereupon all the beneficiaries specified in the notification of acquisition issued under Section 4 of the Act of 1894, become bestowed with a statutory right rather to stake assessment of compensation in accordance with the provisions of the Act of 2013.

12. Bearing in mind the above stated expostulation of law, as made by the Apex Court in the Constitutional Bench verdict rendered in Indore Development case (supra), besides bearing in mind the employment of the above interpretation to the proviso which occurs underneath sub Section 2 of Section 24 of the Act of 2013, thus it has been gauged whether the acquiring authority had rendered an award in respect of the subject lands, thus in terms of the first component of sub Section 2 of Section 24 of the Act of 2013, hence after 5 years or more prior to commencement of the Act of 2013.

Moreover, it has also be fathomed whether rapat possession over the subject lands became assumed by the acquiring authority, before the coming into the 8 of 12 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:085272-DB force of the Act of 2013.
In addition, it has also got to be gauged whether the compensation determined under Section 11 of the Act of 1894, was made available for disbursement thereof, thus to the land-losers concerned.

Significantly, if either of the above become satisfied, thus before coming into the force of the Act of 2013, inasmuch as, either of the two contingencies become satisfied on or before 01.01.2014 i.e. the date when the Act of 2013 assumed force, therebys the non-applicant-petitioner in the instant review application becomes dis-empowered to claim that a lapsing declaration be made vis-a-vis the subject lands.
13. Therefore, the facts relevant for applying the above expostulations of law, do candidly speak, that physical possession of the acquired lands became assumed in the year 25.09.2012.
The said fact is revealed in the reply submitted by U.T., to the main petition.
However, the compensation as become determined under the Act of 1894, become deposited vis-a-vis the non-applicant-petitioner hence on 21.08.2014.
The said date of deposit of the determined compensation as pertains to the present non-applicant-petitioner, thus is post the coming into force of the Act of 2013.

However, in view of the above expostulations of law, wherebys on evident accomplishment of the condition relating to assumption of physical possession over the subject lands, condition whereof became accomplished on 25.09.2012 i.e. the date prior to the coming into force of the Act of 2013.
Resultantly, even if the determined compensation in respect of the non- applicant-petitioner became deposited on 21.08.2014 i.e. on a date, thus post the coming into force of the Act of 2013.

Nonetheless, as Shaheed Baba Jiwan Singh Ji vs U.T Chandigarh And Anr on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7397259/
6 expostulated in the above alluded to paragraphs, the happening of evident assumption of physical possession on 25.09.2012, thus before coming into force of the Act 9 of 12 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:085272-DB of 2013, is a sufficient deterrent against the non-applicant-petitioner rather claiming the making of a lapsing declaration in terms of Section 24(2) of the Act of 2013, de hors, the compensation amount, as determined under the Act of 1894 becoming deposited post the coming into force of the Act of 2013.

sentences.text: 14. The further reason for fortifying the above drawn inference is squarely rooted, on a reading of the proviso which occurs underneath sub Section 2 of Section 24 of the Act of 2013.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in paragraph 172 of the verdict rendered in Indore Development case (supra), paragraph whereof stands extracted hereinafter, has made a declaration of law, that the said paragraph covers a situation where there is assumption of rapat or physical possession of the subject lands, but when the compensation determined under the Act of 1894, has remained unavailable for disbursement to the land-losers concerned, thereupon the beneficiaries or the land-losers concerned, become conferred with an entitlement, as contemplated in the proviso to sub Section 2 of Section 24 of the Act of 2013, but subject to the condition that as contemplated therein, qua their existing cogent evidence, displaying that there was a complete failure on the part of the acquiring authority to deposit the determined compensation, in respect of the major portion or the major chunk of the acquired lands.
"172. A reading of section 24(2) shows that in case possession has been taken even if the compensation has not been paid, the proceedings shall not lapse.

In case payment has not been made nor deposited with respect to the majority of the holdings in the accounts of the beneficiaries, then all the beneficiaries specified in the notification under Section 4 of the Act of 1894 shall get the enhanced compensation under the provisions of the Act of 2013.
Section 24(2) not only deals with failure to take physical possession but also failure to make payment of compensation.
If both things have not been done, there is lapse of the acquisition proceeding.

But 10 of 12 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:085272-DB where payment has been made though possession has been taken or payment has been made to some of the persons but not to all, and it has also not been deposited as envisaged in the proviso
, in that event all beneficiaries (under the same award) shall get higher compensation.
This is because once possession is been taken, there can be no lapse of the proceedings, and higher compensation is intended on failure to deposit the compensation.
Once an award has been passed and possession has been taken, there is absolute vesting of the land, as such higher compensation follows under the proviso, which is beneficial to holders.
In a case where both the negative conditions have not been fulfilled, as mentioned in section 24(2), there is a lapse.

Thus, the proviso, in our opinion is a wholesome provision and is, in fact, a part of section 24(2); it fits in the context of section 24(2)
as deposit is related with the payment of compensation and lapse is provided due to non-payment along with not taking possession for five years or more whereas for non-deposit higher compensation is provided.

Thus, when one of the conditions has been satisfied in case payment has been made, or possession has not been taken,
there is no lapse of the proceedings as both the negative conditions must co-exist."

sentences.text: Therefore, it has to be gauged, whether the acquiring authority did enforce the award made under the Act of 1894, thus through its ensuring that in respect of the major chunk of the subject lands, rather the determined compensation amount becoming remitted into the respective accounts of the land-losers concerned, whose landholdings hence covered the major or a substantial portion of the lands covered within the acquisition notification.

The evidence in respect of the above is comprised in the contention raised by the applicant in the written statement filed to the main writ petition, wherein, it has been stated that the total quantum of the lands, as became subjected to acquisition under the Act of 1894, thus was 229.07 acres, whereas, in respect of 220 acres of lands,
compensation has been released into the accounts of the beneficiaries of the acquisition proceedings.

11 of 12 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:085272-DB 16. Consequently, when in respect of a sizeable or a major chunk of the subject lands, thus the determined compensation has been released into the respective accounts of the land-losers concerned, thus before the coming into force of the Act of 2013, whereas, the area of lands, in respect whereof there is no release of compensation to the non-applicant-petitioner, but is minimal.

Nonetheless, given the interpretation (supra), to the proviso occurring underneath under sub Section 2 of Section 24 of the Act of 2013, thereupon reiteratedly, given the minimality of the landholdings of the present non-applicant-petitioner vis-a-vis the immensity of the size of the holdings of other land-losers concerned, in respect whereof, the determined compensation has been released qua him.

Resultantly, even if the date of deposit of the determined compensation amount as relates to the present non-applicant-petitioner but occurred post the coming into force of the Act of 2013, yet the present non-applicant-petitioner is also not entitled to be assigned the benefit of the proviso which occurs underneath sub Section 2 of Section 24 of the Act of 2013, nor therebys there is any necessity for making a mandamus upon the respondents to determine compensation in respect of the subject lands in accordance with the provisions of the Act of 2013.

17. Disposed of accordingly.
 (SURESHWAR THAKUR)
 JUDGE 10.07.2024 (SUDEEPTI SHARMA)
